headline: Security firm S2W says hundreds of servers worldwide run the same AI hacking tools used in the South Korean financial hacks.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: new threat report of 8 Oct; facts read in full.
importance_line: What changed: the same AI tools run on hundreds of servers, and loan inquiry records leaked from South Korean financial firms could be used in scams against customers; the doubt is that this rests on one firm's report.
summary: SBS News reports, citing a threat report from security firm S2W released on 8 October, that hundreds of servers worldwide run the same open-source AI penetration-testing tools used in recent South Korean financial-sector hacks. It matters because loan inquiry records leaked in those hacks could fuel targeted voice phishing, while S2W found that samples offered in online posts selling millions of customer records had been faked.
notes: Pool URL (Chosun Ilbo) returned no text; SBS article read instead, and credited as the outlet that reported S2W's findings. Article is AI-translated per SBS.
